import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source4_78_1 and Source4_78_0 on Source4_78_1.name == Source4_78_0.school
# Rename Source4_78_0.school to 'name' to join on the same column name or join on left_on/right_on
# We'll join on left: df1.name, right: df0.school
df_joined = pd.merge(df1, df0, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")

# Operation 2: GROUP BY Source4_78_1 columns: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# Aggregations:
# avg(Source4_78_0.Average Math Score) -> Average Math Score (float)
# avg(Source4_78_0.Average Reading Score) -> Average Reading Score (float)
# sum(Source4_78_0.Number Passing Math) -> Number Passing Math (int)
# sum(Source4_78_0.Number Passing Reading) -> Number Passing Reading (int)
# sum(Source4_78_1.size) -> School Size (int)

group_cols = ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']

agg_dict = {
    'Average Math Score': 'mean',
    'Average Reading Score': 'mean',
    'Number Passing Math': 'sum',
    'Number Passing Reading': 'sum',
    'size': 'sum'  # from Source4_78_1, but after join it is duplicated, so we use the joined 'size'
}

grouped = df_joined.groupby(group_cols).agg(agg_dict).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
# 'size' sum aggregation -> 'School Size'
grouped = grouped.rename(columns={'size': 'School Size'})

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema:
# 'School ID': integer
grouped['School ID'] = grouped['School ID'].astype(int)
# 'name': string (object)
grouped['name'] = grouped['name'].astype(str)
# 'type': string (object)
grouped['type'] = grouped['type'].astype(str)
# 'size': integer (original size column in group_cols)
grouped['size'] = grouped['size'].astype(int)
# 'budget': integer
grouped['budget'] = grouped['budget'].astype(int)
# 'Average Math Score': float
grouped['Average Math Score'] = grouped['Average Math Score'].astype(float)
# 'Average Reading Score': float
grouped['Average Reading Score'] = grouped['Average Reading Score'].astype(float)
# 'Number Passing Math': integer
grouped['Number Passing Math'] = grouped['Number Passing Math'].astype(int)
# 'Number Passing Reading': integer
grouped['Number Passing Reading'] = grouped['Number Passing Reading'].astype(int)
# 'School Size': integer
grouped['School Size'] = grouped['School Size'].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema order exactly
target_columns = ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget',
                  'Average Math Score', 'Average Reading Score',
                  'Number Passing Math', 'Number Passing Reading', 'School Size']

result = grouped[target_columns]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 as per hint 21
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source0 on name=school
df_1_0 = pd.merge(source1, source0, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source2 on name=school
df_all = pd.merge(df_1_0, source2, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")

# Group by the primary key columns of the target: School ID, name, type, size, budget
group_cols = ["School ID", "name", "type", "size", "budget"]

# Aggregations:
# Average Math Score: average of math_score from Source2
# Average Reading Score: average of reading_score from Source2
# Number Passing Math: count of students with math_score >= 70 (passing threshold)
# Number Passing Reading: count of students with reading_score >= 70 (passing threshold)
# School Size: sum of size from Source1 (should be same per school, but sum to match target)

agg_df = df_all.groupby(group_cols).agg(
    **{
        "Average Math Score": ("math_score", "mean"),
        "Average Reading Score": ("reading_score", "mean"),
        "Number Passing Math": (lambda x: (x >= 70).sum(), "math_score"),
        "Number Passing Reading": (lambda x: (x >= 70).sum(), "reading_score"),
        "School Size": ("size", "sum"),
    }
)

# The above agg with lambdas needs to be done carefully:
# pandas agg does not support named aggregation with lambdas directly in this way.
# So we do it stepwise:

grouped = df_all.groupby(group_cols)

average_math = grouped["math_score"].mean()
average_reading = grouped["reading_score"].mean()
number_passing_math = grouped.apply(lambda g: (g["math_score"] >= 70).sum())
number_passing_reading = grouped.apply(lambda g: (g["reading_score"] >= 70).sum())
school_size = grouped["size"].sum()

# Combine all into one DataFrame
result = pd.concat(
    [
        average_math.rename("Average Math Score"),
        average_reading.rename("Average Reading Score"),
        number_passing_math.rename("Number Passing Math"),
        number_passing_reading.rename("Number Passing Reading"),
        school_size.rename("School Size"),
    ],
    axis=1,
).reset_index()

# Ensure column order matches target schema exactly
result = result[
    [
        "School ID",
        "name",
        "type",
        "size",
        "budget",
        "Average Math Score",
        "Average Reading Score",
        "Number Passing Math",
        "Number Passing Reading",
        "School Size",
    ]
]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_78/target_multisource_critique_history.csv",
    index=False,
)
